title: O A T P one B one and simvastatin

segs.text: Section seventeen. O A T P one B one and simvastatin. O A T P one B one is the second transporter, newer than P glycoprotein. The gene is S L C O one B one, the protein O A T P one B one. It sits on the sinusoidal membrane of liver cells, not in the gut, and takes weakly acidic drugs and compounds the body makes into the liver: statins, methotrexate, bilirubin. At least forty non synonymous S N Ps are known.

Star five is one S N P, r s four one four nine zero five six, five twenty one T to C, valine one seventy four to alanine. It has reduced function, possibly from reduced expression, and is rare, about one percent. Star fifteen and star seventeen are common, five to fifteen percent in European and Asian populations. They are haplotypes, more than one S N P, each containing the star five S N P plus others, so any two of these alleles give two copies of the star five S N P and count as homozygous.

O A T P one B one takes simvastatin into the liver. A reduced function transporter takes up less, so more simvastatin stays in the plasma. Patients homozygous for the star five S N P have a two hundred twenty one percent increase in simvastatin plasma exposure, area under the curve.

High statin levels cause muscle breakdown, and pain in the large muscles is the warning symptom. In rhabdomyolysis, muscle cell contents enter the blood and damage the kidneys. That is why patients are now often genotyped for star five, fifteen and seventeen. With at least one nonfunctional allele, lower the simvastatin dose or give another statin; some statins cause less rhabdomyolysis, so a different statin may beat a lower dose.
